title: Lightbox
rule: Translucent papers laid one over another: each later beat on a new sheet, all visible at once in fading strength.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
made: a lightbox rendered as transmitted light: lamp-lit glass, then six translucent animation sheets laid in order; each sheet has its own transmittance (0.52), room-light reflection (0.41) and a scatter blur (2.2 px) of everything beneath it, so each earlier beat shows through every later sheet that overlaps it, softer and fainter

HANDMADE sheet paper: cloud and fibre texture generated per sheet (method after the 99-ways-subjective lightbox sheet), three punched peg holes that let the bare light through, tape strips at the top corners, sheet numbers 1-6 in the pen hand
first-person cut-paper hands (black paper, opaque on the box): back of the hand, four fingers and thumb with per-finger curl, forearm out of the bottom of the field; the pencil cut as a tapered strip

the set pen-drawn on each sheet in the shared pen line (desk edge and inkwell, ticket window with TICKET OFFICE, clock at 4:10 with pendulum case, cupboard with its leaf swung on the left jamb, SERVICE door)
the stranger cut from grey tissue behind the window (half transparent); balloons, the memo slip and the SERVICE tags are glued slips of heavier bond, which block more light and read greyer
the ANRC 1922 key cutout (99-ways-template piece) glued down as an opaque piece on its pen hook
folio by pen99.folio on the glass

events.E0: sheet 1: his hands at the desk, the memo slip ('4:15 - open SERVICE door. Key in cupboard.'), pencil in his right hand
events.E1: sheet 2: the stranger in grey tissue behind the TICKET OFFICE window; question balloon; his pencil hand at the edge
events.E2: sheet 3: the clock at 4:10 filling his view; the answer balloon with its tail running off the bottom (his own voice)
events.E3: sheet 4: the window, her shoulder leaving at its right jamb; thanks balloon
events.E4: sheet 5: his left hand on the swung leaf; the cupboard open, the key on its hook, tag SERVICE
events.E5: sheet 6: the key still on its hook, the SERVICE door shut at the right, his pencil hand rising toward his chin; the forgetting balloon from below

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: the sheets are laid on the lightbox one at a time; with each new sheet the earlier beats sink under it and fade

self_check.check: A reader sees earlier beats show through later ones. -> sheet 1's hands show through sheet 3, sheet 3's balloon tail and sheet 5's hand show through sheets 5 and 6, sheet 2's window lines through sheet 4 (maker's judgement from the full-size page; blind reading pending)
self_check.evidence: measured (optics parameters, size) and perceptually judged (from frames) by the maker; independent readers not yet run

weaknesses: first person: the agent is never seen, only his hands; that is the paper-hands medium, but a reader must infer who 'I' is from the memo and the pencil
the fading is by overlap only: where a sheet is not covered it is seen at full strength, so 'fading' shows in the overlaps, not as a uniform dimming of older sheets
the hands are simple cut shapes; at phone width they read as hands but not as specifically his (no sleeve or waistcoat)
sheets 5 and 6 repeat the same cupboard; the change (hand on leaf -> pencil rising, SERVICE door entering) is small
